title: Genomes of the Avar-period elite
fact_summary: Two genetic studies by different teams report that elite Avar-period burials in the Carpathian Basin (7th century) belonged to people with mainly East or Northeast Asian ancestry.

place.label: Great Hungarian Plain
place.note: Pin placed by Claude in the middle of the region the study names ('the Great Hungarian Plain'). It is not the position of any one grave.

claims.text: Gnecchi-Ruscone and colleagues produced genome-wide data from 66 pre-Avar and Avar-period individuals from the Carpathian Basin, including the 8 richest Avar-period burials.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: They report that these individuals “carried Northeast Asian ancestry matching the profile of preceding Mongolian Steppe populations”, particularly a genome from the Rouran period.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: Maróti and colleagues, a different team, sequenced 143 Avar-period samples, 40 of them from the early Avar period (7th century). They report that a mostly elite group among them was derived from East Asia, most likely from present-day Mongolia.

sources.locator: p. 2858; p. 2861; STAR Methods, p. e1

claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: The Avar elite reached the Carpathian Basin through a rapid, long-distance migration from the Mongolian steppe.

held_by.who: Maróti et al. (2022), who say 'most likely from present day Mongolia'

claims.certainty_reason: Two tier B studies from different teams point the same way. Only the abstract of the first was read, and no review has been checked.

claims.text: European Avars were related to the Huns.
claims.certainty_reason: Stated in one tier B study's highlights; the full argument has not been checked.

dating_methods.text: Both studies assign the elite graves to the 7th century.
dating_methods.certainty_reason: Period labels from the studies; the dating evidence for each grave has not been checked.

open_questions.text: Did ordinary people of the Avar period share this ancestry? Maróti and colleagues report that most people in each period were local.

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.
